body: Kenya has many unique Google cars, including those with snorkels and roof racks, useful for Street View identification.
In many Street View coverages, a grey Toyota SUV is seen following the Google car.
Kenya uses long white front licence plates and square yellow rear plates.
The mobile network brand Safaricom is unique to Kenya with locations in almost every city.
Kenyan road lines feature solid white outer lines and yellow inner lines which can be solid or dashed.
Directional signs in Kenya are green with white text and borders, sometimes showing yellow road numbers.
Kenyan road signs are mostly red and white, though they appear infrequently.
County names are often present on signs and billboards, making Kenyan counties knowledge useful for location identification.
Repurposed vans are widespread in Kenya with distinct vehicle wrap designs different from neighboring Uganda.
Eucalyptus trees, identified by long clumped leaves and smooth bark, are commonly found across Kenya.
Some Generation 3 Street View coverage in Kenya shows no visible Google car.
Coverage outside southwest Kenya is mostly limited to main roads.
Kenya’s natural landform varies from flat east and north to higher elevation southwest.
Kenya has distinct regional climates including humid, semi-arid, arid, and very-arid zones.
The Generation 3 grey car with a large snorkel is mostly found in the west and Mombasa/Nairobi areas.
Generation 3 black car with small snorkel appears mostly in the east and near Nairobi.
Kenya mostly has Generation 4 coverage by a large grey Google car with various metas.
White pieces of tape on Google car roof appear north and south of Nairobi.
The A109 between Mombasa and Nairobi has light orange dirt, hills, and many trucks.
Mombasa and coastal towns have white sandy soil, palm trees, and a coastal atmosphere.
Far west Kenya near Kisumu is an agricultural area with farms, grassy hills, and tall eucalyptus.
Kitui area is semi-arid, mountainous with light orange sandy dirt.
Northwest Kenya has limited coverage, tan soil, low trees, and flat to hilly terrain.
Kenya’s National Parks & Reserves feature unique Google cars with snorkels across multiple locations.
The B9 road in the northeast has unpaved reddish-orange dirt and flat terrain with surrounding trees.
The A2 road between Isiolo and Marsabit features plants along the road and large mountains in the distance.
North of Marsabit is much flatter with mountains visible to the south and sparse vegetation.
The A3 north of Garissa has light colored soil and many green trees along the road.
Western C34 is a flat east-west road with sugar cane fields and a mountain range to the north.
A car covered in specks of dirt is unique to certain stretches of the A3, B9, and Habaswein-Dadaab roads.
Nairobi is Kenya’s largest city, with many skyscrapers and dense, developed urban areas.
Mt Kilimanjaro is often visible to the south in coverage north of the mountain, especially near Oloitoktok.
Homa Bay is recognized by its distinctive protruding hill to the east.
Mara Triangle mostly consists of flat or hilly terrain with Generation 4 Google car coverage.
Amboseli National Park features grey cars with snorkels, flat tan grasslands, few trees, and views of Kilimanjaro.
Aberdare National Park car is grey and brown with a large snorkel, often featuring rubber bands on the roof rack.
Between Kitale and Mt Elgon, reddish dirt and greener landscapes differentiate this area from Aberdare.
The Kerio to Lodwar area is sandy, dry with little vegetation, sharing car metas with Aberdare National Park.
North of Kibaoni on the B8 features many succulents alongside the road.
